grammar.topic: Present continuous: now and changing trends
grammar.rule: Use the present continuous (am/is/are + verb-ing) for things happening right now and for changes around us: "Dre IS WEARING a vest right now." "Robots ARE GETTING smarter." Use the simple present for habits: "Dre CUTS hair every day."

exercises.sentence: Look! Dre ___ a vest right now.
exercises.explain: Right now = present continuous: is wearing.
A change that is happening now: are getting.

exercises.sentence: Virginia ___ her work at the moment.
exercises.explain: At the moment = present continuous: is recording.
A habit (every day) = simple present: cuts.

grammar2.topic: Comparatives: -er than, more than, as … as
grammar2.rule: Short adjectives take -er + than: "cheaper than". Use "more" + longer adjectives: "more nimble than". Always say THAN after a comparative (German "als"). For "equally", use as … as: "as hard AS coding" (German "wie").

Cutting hair is as hard ___ coding.
The new robot is ___ than the old one.

true_false.statement: Dre is a barber near Dallas.
true_false.reveal: ✅ TRUE! He cuts hair and records himself at the same time.

true_false.statement: Dre wears a vest with three cameras.
true_false.reveal: ❌ FALSE! The vest has FIVE cameras.

true_false.statement: Dre was worried about the cameras, but Ed was gung ho.
true_false.reveal: ❌ FALSE! Dre was gung ho. Ed was worried at first.
✅ TRUE! She recorded about 10 hours of footage.

true_false.statement: The money paid for two weeks of groceries.
true_false.reveal: ✅ TRUE! It also helped with back-to-school shopping.

true_false.statement: Instawork says it pays below minimum wage.
true_false.reveal: ❌ FALSE! It says it pays well ABOVE minimum wage.

true_false.statement: A critic says the pay is close to the real value of the data.
true_false.reveal: ❌ FALSE! He says it is not close to the real value.

true_false.statement: "Supervision" in English means coaching, like German "Supervision".
true_false.reveal: ❌ FALSE! It means Aufsicht: watching and controlling work. A false friend!

hero.h1: Cameras on the vest. Robots in the lab. Are these workers training robots to replace themselves?

page.videoTitle: Are These Workers Training Robots to Replace Them?
page.vidTip: 🎧 Listen for 3 things: cameras, worried, new jobs. (It’s only 4 minutes! No time? You can skip.)
page.vidEnd: Dre’s big question: will training robots help or hurt workers?
page.wpEnd: Say them out loud: “annotate the footage”, “deploy a robot”…
page.slipEnd: Typical slips: “cuts” for right now, “cheap than”, “more as”, “as … than”.

ice.title: Robot or Human?
ice.tip: 👉 Is it a robot job, a human job or both? Pick a card. Then we tell you our ruling!
cards: Robots already do this: millions of robot vacuums clean homes every day.
Robots have helped to build cars for decades.
For now, this is a human job. Most people do not want a robot near their ears! ✂️
Both: robots can carry things, but patients need a caring human.
Machines are learning it, but a human still does it best.
Both: software checks the numbers, the advisor makes the decision.
results: You see things differently from us. Today’s story may change your mind!
You agree with us on most jobs.
You and our ruling think alike!

read.txt: Dre is a barber near Dallas. Every day he cuts hair, and a vest with five cameras records him. This [[footage]] goes to a tech company, and the company uses it to teach robots. So Dre does one job and gets paid twice. That is a big [[incentive]]. Dre is now a [[gig worker]] too: he takes small, separate jobs for different companies.
read.q: Why does Dre wear the cameras?
read.fb: For extra money: one job, two payments.

read.txt: Dre was [[gung ho]]: very excited. His friend Ed was not. Ed thought, “This will take our jobs!” Then he changed his mind. Now Ed wears a [[rig|camera rig]] too, because he does not want to [[get left behind]].
read.fb: Ed was worried. Dre was gung ho.

read.txt: Today’s robots are more [[nimble]] than ever, because AI is making them smarter. But there is a [[bottleneck]]: good data. So workers like Virginia, a nail tech, record hours of their work. Then people [[annotate]] the video: they add labels, so the robots can learn. Virginia gets paid above [[minimum wage]], and the money paid for two weeks of groceries.
read.q: What is the bottleneck for robots?
read.fb: Data. Robots learn from human work, and that data is hard to get.

read.txt: A critic is not happy. He says the pay is far below the real value of the data. Robots will soon be cheaper than people, he says, and then companies can [[deploy]] them for every job. The robots will [[stick around]] forever, and the workers will not. The company disagrees: robots still need human [[supervision]], and new jobs such as robot [[wrangle|wrangling]] will appear.
read.q: What does the company say about the future?
read.fb: The company says people will still be needed, and new jobs will come.
